div.ab:
Again, a composite interpretation of David, king and prophet. The first Psalm. Blessed the man, (v.1) i.e. They are a kingdom, mansions of light, something that eye has not seen and ear has not heard. Man is mentioned alone because the nature of man and woman are one, and from that part which is more excellent he designates the whole. That in the way of the wicked (v.1) i.e. of the murderers and oppressors. Not does he walk, (v.1) i.e. not did he say: he is not walking, because it is not known whether he that is alive is a saint. To him, therefore, that completes his way in holiness and (to him that) walks in excellence is given bliss. And in the council of the sinners, (v.1) i.e. sinners he calls fornicators, adulterers and the intemperate. And upon the seat of the mockers, (v.2) i.e. the wicked that mock God and his incarnation. Further, the wicked and the sinners and the mockers are the scribes and the Pharisees and the teachers of the law. And the faculty of walking he calls the soul, standing (he calls) the mind, sitting (he calls) the body; the way (he calls) that evil that captivates the mental and sensual faculties so that, if a man does not repudiate evil, he shall not be worthy of bliss. Further, the wicked he calls the idol-worshippers. He gives bliss not to him that does not commit sin, as an animal or a stone, but to him whose delight is in the law of the Lord; meditation of divine delight pertains to rational (beings). A sinner he calls him in whom is faith and who rejects
the moral way of life. The seat of the mockers, (v.2) i.e. the seat he calls the teaching of those who transgress the law, who are lying teachers, who proclaim of themselves the priesthood and not of the Holy Spirit. But in the law of the Lord, (v.2) i.e. who meditates in the law day and night, i.e. with constant application. He meditates day and night, (v.2) i.e. day he calls the good intention and the just execution in which he shines.

Night he calls the bodily application which, even though it is occupied with the care of the body, does not fall from the true enlightenment. Further, the law he calls the gospel or the natural (law) by which saints and morals were directed before Moses. Day and night, (v.2) i.e. when we happen upon joy, which he calls day, and also upon trials, which he names night, it is meet that we meditate in the law. He shall be as tree, (v.3) i.e. on account of the wood, i.e. tree he calls the Messiah as (we read) wood of life is he to those that hold fast to him and continue in him. River of water, (v.3) i.e. baptism or a life-giving doctrine. Therefore, wood of life is the Messiah to those who confess him. River of water, i.e. gushing forth the sense of divine writings. His fruit he gives, (v.3) i.e. the fruit of the trees are forgiveness of sins, universal salvation, the miracles that the Lord did. His foliage does not fall, (v.3) i.e. the doctrines and the dogmas and the commandments because, whoever believes and keeps the commandments, not shall his leaves fall by those winds by which are allegorically meant the trials. Everything he does, succeeds, (v.3) i.e. to the end he perseveres unshaken. Not thus are the wicked, (v.4) i.e. even
though they are wealthy and prominent in this world, yet like chaff that the wind carries away, they go away and they go and they are not, and because they are straw, they fall in the fire. Further, because they are addicted to wickedness, they do not want to become grain, and they are in themselves only an image of dust; however, in the image of chaff which is most contemptible, they are thrown from the earth when an evil wind blows upon them. Others (say): the wind of trials blew among the Jews and scattered them and destroyed their cities. Therefore the wicked shall not stand in the judgment, (v.5) i.e. not are they worthy to stand before the tribunal, because they have committed many wicked things and are not like the sinners and the wicked, who are judged and separated from the just. Further, not shall they stand because they have not root and no firm hold, and not shall they be worthy of the investigation, but shall be delivered at once to torment. Neither sinners in the congregation of the righteous, (v.5) i.e. because they shall not enter with them the bridal chamber. Further, if one has sinned and repented a little or under compulsion, even though he enter the kingdom, yet not shall there be one mansion; a different (mansion) is that one of the perfect from that of the hirelings and servants because the wicked and the sinners have not brought excellent fruit. Therefore, in the time of judgment not shall they stand in the midst of the righteous or in their order and in their grade, because the Lord knows the way, (v.6) i.e. it is a straight one and that one from which they enter the narrow gate, until they have purged themselves. The Lord knows them that are his, so that he makes them
inherit praise. The way he calls any way of life that guides the righteous. The way of the wicked shall perish, (v.6) i.e. because it is broadened with passions, it perishes, for the wicked will not be worthy to be in the knowledge of God. When he looks upon the way of the wicked, it vanishes, like the way, i.e. the discipline of the Jews came to an end. For destruction is the end of evil deeds.

Psalm 2: Why do the heathen rage? (V.1). The Greek: snort. In the Hebrew this and the previous one are written as one psalm; in the Greek, however, as two, and in the Acts likewise: in the first it is written that it was said: My son art thou. And furthermore, in the Hebrew the number is not written over the psalm. Snorting is an irrational state of mind (and) an irrational modulation of the voice. The nations are the devil and the demons, the priests and the crucifiers. Snorting is rightfully said of horses, and it is a certain meaningless sound which is mixed with breath, which procedes through the nostrils of these and they produce this when they flee from the comfortable ease of them that feed them. Thus also did the Jews when they rejected the peace which (comes) through the Messiah. And they snorted when they blurted out that Beelzebub was casting out the demons. Further: Why do they snort, i.e. exalt themselves, i.e. these. From pride the nations came to the cult of idols. And nations imagine vain things, (v.1) i.e. they did not
accept our Savior, but crucified him. The kings of the earth rise up, (v.2) i.e. for verily there were assembled in the city against the Holy One, thy Son, Herod and Pilate and the demons. And the rulers, heads, i.e. Hanas and Caiphas. Against the Lord and his Anointed, (v.2) i.e. against the Father and the Son, because the contumely of the Son rises to the Father. Let us cast off their bonds, (v.3) i.e. the yoke of the law in which they were harnessed, for they loosened and cast themselves from the yoke of God and he began to harness in their place oxen, the apostles. Let us undo from us their yoke, (v.3) i.e. lest furthermore the people of God be subjugated in the service of animal sacrifices. He that dwells in the heaven shall laugh, (v.4) i.e. they will be a laughing-stock not only to the nations, but also to God because they planned the stupid thing and sought by the cross to kill the Messiah, and these (words are not said) as though the Lord were rejoicing according to the proper sense of laughter, but also when he shows his anger and wrath. Then he will speak against them in his anger, (v.5) i.e. when the kingdom was taken from them and given to a people that brings fruit. And they were taken captive in the days of Vespasian and Titus, and they were dispersed in all the world. I have established my king over Zion, (v.6) i.e. the Father has established his Son as king over Zion when he sent him and he came to be of a woman and he ruled over the spiritual Zion, i.e. the church on earth and the heavenly one of souls and when the Father called out: This is my Son, and in the temple: I have glorified
him, and again: I will glorify him. Zion, i.e. a watch-tower that is elevated and high. That he might discourse upon my covenant, (v.7) i.e. the New Covenant makes known the holy trinity to men. In the Greek: I stand (as) king is written, i.e. by nature he is king over everything and over the believers of his own free will (i.e. is he king). The Lord said to me: Thou art my Son,, (v.7) i.e. he is eternal, i.e. in the flesh. And this day have I begotten thee, (v.7) i.e. because he did not begin and will not end. Ask of me and I will give thee, (v.8) i.e. not because he needs (anything), for all things that are the father's are his, but because he is human, he asks as one needing and taking, making himself one of the family of mankind. Nations for thine inheritance, (v.8) i.e. that they may be heirs of the kingdom. With a staff of iron, (v.9) i.e. with the word of God which is quick and sharper than a sword, by which the apostles bound and loosed, shepherded and guided. And like the vessels of a potter, (v.9) i.e. the nations of old (he shall break) in whom there was no use because, though they were composed of dust and dust was their appearance and food for the serpent, yet they were purged and washed in baptism. Now, kings understand, (v.10) i.e. salvation through provident guidance. Be instructed, O judges of the earth, (v.10) i.e. in evangelical admonition, entering the narrow gate of repentance and fearing the Messiah. Kiss the son, (v.12) i.e. the eternal one and him who for our sakes became man. For he rejoices in the kiss of penitents as (e.g.) in that of the sinning woman. Further, place
thy mouth upon his dust and eat it since thou art worthy. Lest he be angry, (v.12) i.e. in the judgment to come. And ye perish from his way, (v.12) i.e. the evangelical one. And in a little while his anger will burn, (v.12) i.e. you will burn in unquenchable fire. Blessed are all that trust in him, (v.12) i.e. those that keep his commandments, he will make heirs of bliss. Start from the beginning. Let us cast off their bonds, (v.3) i.e. he commands that we cast off the fetters of idols and demons and sin. He will speak against them in his anger, (v.5) i.e. in the world to come, in his anger he will torment those that do not repent here. I have established my kind, (v.6) i.e. not is it: I have taken a kingdom for myself, for this (that he says) I indicates that not of myself is this, but God has chosen me, anointed me and established me for headship upon Zion. Zion I will remember because of the mystery that is in it. For there Adam was buried and after the flood Shem brought the skull there, and Melchisedek lived there, and Abraham built an altar upon it, and it is declared a look-out place because of its height. Further, though by nature he is king like God, the Father, he was born; (and then) he was established king when he became a human being. The Lord said to me: My son art thou, (v.7) i.e. to him that always was from eternity and the eternal son, he says: I, today, have begotten thee, (v.7) i.e. justly this is said of him: today. In the latter days he became a human being. Hence this (that he says) my son art thou, indicates that at all times and eternally he is with him who begot him and this (that he says) today I have begotten thee, indicates the present time, i.e. in (the time of)
his incarnation. Ask of me and I will give, (v.8) i.e. humanly he says that he was asking and taking, though he is king and God. The gentiles for thine inheritance, (v.8) i.e. because Israel, the former inheritance, acted wickedly toward him, he will take the gentiles for his flock. For neither Zerubbabel nor David nor Solomon took the ends of the earth, but it refers to the Lord that his gospel and faith in him conquers in all the world. Thy possession .. the ends of the earth, (v.8) i.e. the possession of the Messiah, i.e. the kingdom is the end of the earth; of course, the end of earthly rule. Thou wilt shepherd them with a rod of iron, (v.9) i.e. when the people had been rejected, the gentiles entered so that with a rod of iron the people was shepherded, i.e. with wrath capable of crushing, for they were brought into complete subjection by the Roman armies. Like potters vessels thou wilt break them, (v.9) i.e. it is meet to castigate ourselves with works, as (we read) a broken heart God will not reject in order that, when the soul is contrite, it might be a sacrifice to God. Furthermore, the Jews were broken and crushed so that nothing useable was left them. O kings, understand, (v.10) i.e. accept understanding since he that was crucified arose from the place of the dead, and repent of your sins. Be instructed, O judges of the earth, (v.10) i.e. to instruction and teaching surrender yourselves, O judges. Serve the Lord with fear, (v.11) i.e. with trembling and repentance and not with boldness lest the joy of God descend (to a level) with the joy of the world.

Psalm 3: O Lord, how are my oppressors increased, (v.1) i.e. Absalom and Ahithophel. Many are they that rise against me, (v.1) i.e. the demons and the associates of Absalom. You
have no salvation in your God, (v.2) i.e. God is not forgiving his sin which he had sinned against Uriah. And he answered me from his holy hill, (v.4) i.e. heaven. I laid down, (v.5) i.e. in sin. I was awakened, (v.5) i.e. when I rise up in repentance. Not will I fear the multitude of (the people), (v.6) i.e. those that are opposed. The teeth of the wicked, (v.7) i.e. the tyrannical power of the wicked that crushes me. This psalm is understood spiritually of the human nature which was delivered over to the demons and cried out and was sacrificed through the Messiah. Lord, how are increased, (v.1) i.e. the oppressors are the demons and the Jews. Many are they that say, (v.2) i.e. if thou art the Son of God, come down; he trusted in God, let him deliver him. And he answered me from the hill of (his holiness), (v.4) i.e. Golgotha upon which he was sacrificed and sanctified the sinners. For he was answered by God because he had been crucified and had remitted the sin of Adam and had restored him to Eden. I laid down and slept, (v.5) i.e. I died. And I awakened, (v.5) i.e. I arose after three days. I laid down, (v.5) i.e. because he is God, he said: I and not another, as: I have power over my life to lay it down. The Lord sustained me, (v.5) i.e. as we read: the Father raised the Son. Not do I fear, (v.6) i.e. the mob of the Jews and demons that say: crucify him. They surrounded me and arrayed themselves
against me, (v.6) i.e. the guards, lest I be stolen. Arise, O Lord, my God, (v.7) i.e. these (words) he spoke instead of Adam; and if to the Father you apply them, they will not fail. He was praying: my Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Because thou hast smitten, (v.7) i.e. the demons when he delivered the captivity from their hands. The teeth of the wicked, (v.7) i.e. of death and sheol that they further not dare to destroy human nature. To the Lord belongs salvation, (v.8) i.e. to God who was incarnated and not who was made God. Upon thy people will thy blessing (be), (v.8) i.e. upon him who believes; he is blessed when he is free from the curse.

Psalm 4: When I called upon thee, thou answeredst me, (v.1) in this he teaches that he was answered by God and saved from Saul. Know that the Lord hath set apart for himself........ (v.3) i.e. I was anointed king when I was a youth, and not was I an adversary of God because I rose up against Saul. Be angry and sin not, (v.4) i.e. putting evil thoughts into effect, and if it is impossible to keep from being angry, prove the anger ineffectual, and let not the sun set upon it, nursing it for revenge. Sacrifice sacrifices, (v.5) i.e. when you are making ineffectual the evil passions and anger, then you are offering up sacrifices of righteousness. Many are they who say: who will show us............. (v.6) i.e. because the righteous fervently longed to see him who was good by nature because they know that he was about to be incarnated. (Who) will shed upon us the light of his countenance?, (v.6) i.e. his gospel message by which the
living and dead are saved. Lord thou hast given thy joy....... (v.7) i.e. in the remembrance of thy advent and thy salvation my heart rejoices; he made known the time of joy, that is to say, the advent and thy salvation, as if of old he had seen it. At the time of their grain and wine........ (v.7) i.e. with these three sacraments God enriched his church, that is to say, by the body and the blood and the anointing with chrism. (They) are many in peace together, (v.7) i.e. great has become the feast of the church in all the regions and peoples because it proclaims peace and prosperity to everyone. I will lie down and I will sleep, (v.8) i.e. David, because he was not about to see them. In safety thou wilt cause me to dwell, (v.8) i.e. when thou callest me from sheol to paradise.

Psalm 5: Give ear to my words, O Lord, (v.1) i.e. he is praying that he may go out from the law, symbolized by the night, and may come to the epiphany of the son, symbolized by the dawn. And consider my sighing, (v.1) i.e. the constant sighing of my reflexions upon thy wonders. At dawn I will prepare myself and will appear before thee, (v.3) i.e. in the epiphany of Immanuel, the very light of the world whom he calls the dawn. I will appear before thee, (v.3) i.e. in the son we see the father and he is the way and by him we come to the father. Because the proud shall not stand, (v.5) for workers of deceit, (v.5) and wicked liars and shedders of blood,(v.6) he calls the crucifiers because they were cast out from the inheritance. But
I, in the multitude of thy mercy...... (v.7) i.e. the prophet and the rest of the prophets and the believers. I shall worship in thy temple, (v.7) i.e. in the Jerusalem above. In their mouth there is no righteousness, (v.9) i.e. because they shouted with their mouth: we have no king but Caesar. Open sepulchres are their throats, (v.9) i.e. because they were dead in sin, there issues from their mouths a storm of abuse and murder of our Savior. Their tongues are perverted, (v.9) i.e. with a great variety of evil words, as (we read): you are like whitened sepulchres. May they fall by their counsels, (v.10) i.e. the counsel of the fathers, and they are not worthy of rest below or above. May all that trust in thee rejoice in thee, (v.11) i.e. the gentiles rejoice in him instead of the people because they believe in him and are clothed with hir through water and spirit and they put him on and they have, as it were, a shield against the spiritual and the visible enemies.

Psalm 6: Lord in thy anger do not rebuke me, (v.1) i.e. in this he is praying for himself and for all the children of Adam. For not from rebuke am I fleeing but from that (rebuke) which is in anger. Nor in thy wrath......... (v.1) i.e. not from disciplining am I seeking remission but from that (disciplining) which is in wrath, as punishment and not as for correction. Because I am ill, (v.2) i.e. with the sin of transgressing the commandment. My bones tremble, (v.2) i.e. from the curse and the land of thorns. But thou, O Lord, how long?, (v.3) i.e.
not are you solicitous about the human race that the demons have subjugated. Furthermore, bones he calls the powers of the soul: knowledge, fortitude, sobriety, righteousness. Save my soul, (v.4) i.e. from sin. For thy goodness sake, (v.4) i.e. by that (goodness) by which thou hast made us when we did not exist. In death there is no remembrance of thee, (v.5) i.e. that (death) which is after the resurrection in sheol in which one suffers torment; he does not allude to natural death but to the second (death). I am weary with my groanings, (v.6) i.e. from this fear. I water all the night........, (v.6) i.e. the bed he calls reflextion; the coverlet (he calls) thoughts. The mind, that is put at ease in thoughts, prepares the way for sleep to become ours, so that, when I am well washed, I put sordid thoughts away. From all my enemies, (v.7) i.e. the demons and the evil thoughts. Doers of deceit, (v.8) the same ones. Because the Lord has heard, (v.8) i.e. he heard him and is ready to hear him, since he saves all men and accepts their penitence.

Psalm 7: Lord God, in thee have I trusted; deliver me, (v.1) i.e. it is said concerning the words of that Benjaminite, Hushai, who was sent by David to Absalom, and he said to him: it is not meet that you should wage war with thy father. Ahithopel counseled him: pursue him! Lest like a lion, (v.2) i.e. and it is known that it is the devil. Lord, my God, if I have done this, (v.3) may there be such and such to me. According to Andreas, the same psalm: concerning the words of Hushai, the
Benjaminite; in the book of the Kings, Hushai Bar Arek is written the Arkite; for when he went and made to no effect the plan of Ahithopel with eloquent and powerful reasons, he is called the Jaminite. Lord, my God, in thee have I trusted, (v.1) i.e. in thee have I trusted and not in man or in thoughts and counsels and by thee have I been persuaded that I might be saved from my pursuers. Deliver me, (v.1) i.e. what is the difference that he asks to be delivered and afterwards to be saved? The weak are in need of salvation, those that are held in captivity (are in need) of deliverance. Save me from weakness and deliver me from captivity. For those that here contend with demons shall escape from their pursuers. And when they die, they will be examined by the devil, whether they have some small sins. Because of this the prophet says: save me! -that is to say: here from those that pursue me; deliver me, Lord, in that time of examination, lest there snatch me away the lion that is the archon; hence the lion is the devil. Man is called a fierce and brute lion when he ceases to have his rational nature and snatches away like a lion. So the devil snatches away the erring souls. Lord God, if I have done this, (v.3) i.e. he sheds tears when he says that he has not returned to anyone evil for evil. For not have I done such as this, which, behold, now I am feeling. If there is iniquity in my hands, (v.3) i.e. if I have snatched away wealth and the kingdom of someone, may I fall by my worthless enemies; that is to say, if I have done one of these things, may I fall, being worthless and ridiculed by the enemies. May the enemy pursue my soul, (v.5) i.e. the soul of man writhes before
Satan, being trodden under foot. May he stamp down in the earth my life, (v.5) i.e. and with his feet stamping in to the earth, that is to say: into the body (he is stamping) the life of him who falls into sin, and even though these were said by David in the person of Absalom, yet they refer to the devil who, when he pursues our soul, crushes and treads it down into earthly affairs when he sees it unoccupied. May my glory dwell in the dust, (v.5) i.e. the holy have their glory in heaven; even though they are of dust, it is said that their glory dwells in heaven. He that trusts in riches and passing honor, his glory is on the earth. The prophet adds a curse: would that now be about to become dust those things, that are our glory. Arise, Lord, in thy anger, (v.6) i.e. arise, extending thy hand to the oppressed. This (that he says) arise, is to say: from the grave, in anger against the Jews who deny the resurrection. Arise upon the necks of my enemies, (v.6) LXX: be exalted over the boundary. The LXX: rise against, that is to say: be raised upon the wood of the cross so that the demons may be shorn of their power. Awake concerning me in the judgment that thou hast commanded, (v.6) i.e. arise and enforce thy commandment which is scorned. Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousnessof works he alludes and not to that in words. For not have I acted wickedly against Absalom and Ahithopel and the rest. May evil upon the wicked come to an end, (v.9) i.e. may there be an end and a finish of evil and a destruction of the evil of sins.. Thou shalt establish the righteous, (v.9) i.e. the firmness and steadfastness of the righteous. He searches the heart
and the reins, (v.9) i.e. the reins he calls the thoughts because the reins arouse the desires that are below the belly and from here the thoughts of desire set in motion. He foretells the death of Ahithopel. Again he calls the reins the intellectual powers of the soul, for it knows the hidden things like God. He has whetted his sword, (v.12) i.e. his spear he will furbish, that is to say: for he does not use the spear against those that sin. He furbishes it for a time in order that it might serve for a change of heart for those that sin. The implements of wrath, (v.13) i.e. the angels he calls the tormentors. His arrows he has made........, (v.13) i.e. the implements of death. The sword and bow and arrows teach the various kinds of torments, that is to say: those powers which judges bring to bear in proportion to the sin of everyone. Arrows he calls the torments. Burning........, (v.13) i.e. those that burn with the fire of voluptuous desires; against these he prepares arrows so that out of fear they may flee from the torment, and when they extinguish the fire of voluptuous desire, they will escape the fire of hell. He travailed with iniquity, he conceived deceit, etc., (v.14) i.e. when therefore the Jews had travailed, that is to say: conceived iniquity, they gave birth to deceit, for they killed the Messiah. Again he travailed with iniquity, i.e. he travailed, that is to say: the devil conceived Absalom and then gave him birth, making manifest his iniquity, as (we read) he that commits sin, is begotten of the evil one. Before the eyes of everyone he manifested himself as one who opposes his father. May his iniquity return upon his head, (v.15) i.e. Ahithopel, seeing that the adventure of Absalom had come to an end, knew that he would fall under the hand of
David, and therefore he ended his life by a noose in a house. And upon his pate his iniquity........, (v.15) i.e. not upon the limbs of the wicked does the torment come, but upon the head, which being destroyed, the whole body becomes detestable. Iniquity then he calls here that torment because of the iniquity, that descends upon the pate, that is to say: the head.

From the third Psalm: Lord, how many are my oppressors, (v.1) i.e. Absalom waged war with his father and David, seeing the plot of many with his son, feared like a man. Many are they that rise against me, (v.1) i.e. not only Absalom, but also the other rebels who were with him. Why do those whom I have not wronged, run against me with evil? Thus the devil rose against the kingdom of the Messiah. There will not be deliverance for him, (v.2) i.e. because he had sinned against Uriah, God had withdrawn himself from him. Thus also the Jews cried out: if he is the son of God, let him come down from the cross. My glory and the lifter up of my head, (v.3) i.e. David trusted that by this, when he would be helped, he would be honored by God and elevated and would return to the kingdom. He answered me from his hill, (v.4) i.e. heaven, or the altar, or the heart of him who prays is a holy mountain when it cogitates nothing evil, or Golgatha is the mountain which is the bridal-chamber of the bridegroom and the throne of the king.

From the fourth Psalm: In the psalm(s) (is) an ode.
A psalm is praise with the instrument called kenara; an ode is a song concerning victory, or in a psalm he alludes to the practice of one who leads a practical life; an ode (alludes to) him who praises theoretically. When I called upon thee, thou answeredst me, (v.1) i.e. (as we read): while thou are yet speaking, he says: Lo, here am I, and: O sons of men, how long (will you be) heavy-hearted? (v.2) i.e. to those (he speaks) who obscure their understanding; how long will you be heavy-hearted i.e. to those he is speaking who obscure their understanding. How long will you remain in your sins and not repent? Know (that) the Lord has glorified his holy one, (v.3) i.e. (he speaks) of the Messiah whom the Father glorified in every land by the faith of the heathen by means of the mighty things and the miracles that he did. Be angry and sin not, (v.4) i.e. because they were going out to war against Absalom. Those that were angry and incensed at the insurrection of the son against the father, he admonishes to constrain (their anger. Again he commands us to be incensed over evil deeds and voluptuous desires. Anger, such as this, is a preventative against that which is sinful. Upon your beds meditate, (v.4) while you are upon your beds in quietude by yourselves, repent, in calling to mind those things that were done by you
during the day. Repent and be contrite concerning what you have done. Why upon the beds? Because then the meditations are more pure, being free of earthly affairs. Offer up sacrifices of righteousness, (v.5) i.e. not those of the law, but those of the gospel. Again, he that brings an offering from the profits of wickedness, and he that does not distribute, as is meet, to the needy, and he that gives under pressure or by force, does not bring a sacrifice of righteousness. Again sacrifice refers to the sacrifice of the Only-begotten. A sacrifice of righteousness he calls the cross because sinners are made righteous by it. The light of his countenance......, (v.6) i.e. the Messiah is the countenance of the Father. And the light of the countenance, i.e. is the crucified Messiah by which also a light on a candlestick shines upon the world, which we with diligence mark upon our foreheads. Thou hast given thy joy into my heart, (v.7) i.e. (of) one (kind) is the joy of the heart, of another is the joy of the flesh. For the flesh rejoices in eating, the heart, however, in teachings, that is to say, the meditation in theories.

From the fifth Psalm: In the end concerning the heir, that is to say, in the end the praise of the inheritance which is sung concerning the soul or the church which are brought to the divine inheritance, as (we read): come, enter, inherit the kingdom. This in the end (he says) because he refers to the time
of the coming of the Messiah, because the Jews, the heirs over against the heathen, were spurned. They did not abide by my covenant and therefore I have spurned them, says Jeremiah. Hear, O Lord, and consider my anguish, (v.1) i.e. this consider (means) investigate and examine the intent of my crying that I am not asking any human things. Consider is known. Crying refers to the groaning which is in the mind. Because to thee I am praying, (v.2) i.e. he does not say before thee but to thee in order to show his nearness to God. Lord, in the dawn thou shalt hear, (v.3) i.e. in the time of the incarnation, this he calls the dawn. Furthermore, in the light of virtue, for when we shall cease from the darkness of sin, then we will bring an acceptable prayer to the sun of righteousness. Those that are ignorant of morals, he names the servants of lawlessness, (v.5), those that hate God (v.5) (he names) those that fall away from the truth; those that speak lies (v.6) (he names) those that God destroys (v.6). The devil is a speaker of lies; he and his adherents perish. Again speakers of lies, (v.6) i.e. it is meet that we judge him that lies by the intent and not by the utterance. For, behold, Rahab lied to them that were searching for the spies, and she is not classed among those that perish or among the lying. And thus is not everyone that kills a murderer. For those that kill a man according to the law, as Samuel and
Elijah killed, are not called murderers or men of blood, although they killed the wicked. A man of blood and the deceitful the Lord will repudiate, (v.6) i.e. here he puts on the same level the murderer and deceitful person; for what the murderer does with the hand, the deceitful person does with the tongue; the one is in need of time and a place to commit murder, the other commits every evil with words. In the multitude of thy goodness I will enter......, (v.7) i.e. I have no virtue that brings me to God, but by thy mercy, I will enter thy house. I will worship in thy holy temple (v.7) with fear, (v.8) i.e. it is meet that we enter the church with fear, knowing that we are to converse with God in prayer. Therefore let us worship with fear and not with mocking and with bodily adornment let us enter the church. Because of my enemies make the way straight before me, (v.8) i.e. he who seeks to think and act uprightly has many enemies, demons and jealous men, seeking after the goods of him who admonishes. When the prophet sees this, he asks God to help him from the harms of the evil one. In thy fear, O Lord, lead me and in thy righteousness, (v.8) i.e. righteousness he calls the Messiah
by whom, as by a shepherd, he is led. Because of my enemies...., (v.8) i.e. the demons he names the enemies and prays that the way may be straightened before him that he may not be harmed by them. There is no righteousness in their mouth, (v.9) i.e. truth, i.e. the externally wise and the heretics and Satan who deceived Adam. But iniquity is in them, (v.9) i.e. the Greek: their heart is empty, like their words; their thoughts themselves contemplate vain and superfluous things. Their throats are open sepulchres, (v.9) i.e. the throats of the evil he names sepulchres their teeth (he names) worms, bringing forth dead bones for words. Deceitful (v.9) we find to be sheol according to the order of the figure of speech. Again the graves, that are closed, cover in them, as is fitting, the odor; those that are open emit the evil odor and harm others. Words of blasphemy and shamelessness like these they spew forth. Hold them guilty O God, (v.10) i.e. judge them, O God, condemn them and help those that are oppressed. Cast them out, (v.10) i.e. because they have withdrawn from thee, throw them out; because they have rebelled against thee, (v.10) i.e. for God does not fall under our passions; ours are considered his by analogy. Thus also when he speaks of error, as (we read): I have led astray thy sons, and (when he speaks) of not knowing, as (we read): I do not know you.
Because of us he says these things, for he is removed from provocation and error and hatred. Because thou wilt bless the righteous, (v.12) i.e. in order that they obtain heavenly blessings. Lord, as with armor of good pleasure thou crownest......, (v.12) i.e. the armor of the cross is the crown; the armor (is) for the warriors and the soldiers; the crown for the victors. Good pleasure he names the love of humanity for oursakes: it pleased him to save us sinners.

From the sixth Psalm. The eighth refers to the latter day of resurrection because on the seventh day the works of the world were finished; on the eighth the creation is at an end. Because my bones are moved, (v.2) i.e. bones he names thoughts because through them the living being is held upright. The agitation of these perturbs and agitates me. Therefore the powers of the soul are the bones that are agitated and because of this he adds: and my soul is moved very much, (v.3) i.e. for when the powers of the soul are perturbed, so the soul (is perturbed). When it falls into voluptuousness (es) and desires and splendors, it is agitated, and when it is tossed into this storm, then the bones, that is to say, the powers of the mind are perturbed. Thou, O Lord, how long? (v.3) i.e. the Lord delays the healing of him who prays in order that he may remain in the possession of the eternal blessings. Return, O Lord, and deliver it, (v.4) i.e.
it is characteristic of shepherds to turn the sheep from going astray; therefore turn, that is to say, convert and save my soul, that is with demons in error and in need of liberation by thee. In death there is no one who remembers thee, (v.5) i.e. not is any one able to keep thy commandments there; and let us do good, for after death there will not be room for renewal. This present time is that of restoration and not that of the future. In sheol who will profess thee, (v.5) i.e. for the judge will not accept profession there. I am weary with my groanings and flood my bed all the night, (v.6) i.e. for the one night of sin I will purify my soul every night afterwards with tears of repentance. He professes that he will love works and not love a life of ease, but will increase repentance, and sobbing, he will weary himself to establish the wearying of evil, and he teaches that he will not make the night a time of respite and sleep like the animals, but of waking and good deeds. Furthermore, and with my tears I water my coverlet, (v.6) i.e. the bed and the coverlet with which I committed sin, I am washing by means of tears. Again no one will water the bed and the coverlet, in the material sense of the words, and this all the night crying, but the bed is the mind and the coverlet (is) the thoughts. My eye is terrified with anger, (v.7) i.e. the eye of the soul is the thought of the mind which is perturbed and agitated by anger. I grow old with
all my enemies, (v.7) i.e. the enemies he calls the demons because we grow old through evils, we are crushed by demons. Again enemies he calls the thoughts of voluptuousness(es) because of which our Lord says: the enemies of a man are the sons of his house, by which we grow old as by moths. Depart from me all ye workers of iniquity, (v.8) i.e. these (words) were said to the demons who rejoiced in his fall; when he arose from sin he rebuked them. Because the Lord heard the voice of my crying, (v.8) i.e. as is the voice of sin, so also that of repentance; not of the voice of the lips does he speak, but of that which comes from the deeds of repentance. May they be ashamed and perturbed, (v.10) and the rest, i.e. he urges upon God that with the casting out of the demons from him, also disgrace may bepoured out upon them when they see that their deception was ineffective.

The psalm according to the catena of Zōura. The beginning of the seventh psalm, behold it is written above in the two previous folios. Turn back and combine the foregoing with this. Arise, Lord, in thy anger, (v.6) and with this he asks that the Lord may appear in the flesh. Awake for me in the judgment that thou hast commanded, (v.6) i.e. through the forefathers he promised that he would save us and judge Satan. And the congregation of the nations will surround thee, (v.7) i.e. because he
is about to do this and to call the nations, he says, that not one nation, as theretofore, but many nations will turn to God. Because of this return on high, (v.7) i.e. having descended, thou hast ascended from the vexation in the flesh to heaven again. Evil upon the wicked......, (v.9) i.e. the demons. The righteous God, (v.10) God that saves, (v.10) God judges, (v.11) i.e. an indication that there are three persons: God who saves and judges and is righteous. He is not angry every day but turns, (v.11) i.e. at the church he is not angry as against the synagogue. He has whetted his sword, (v.12) and the rest of the words he directs against the devil who waged war against the church, but was vanquished when the word was made flesh and he fell into the pit that he had made, (v.15). He made his arrows ......, (v.13) i.e. the punishment to come and the fire that is not quenched.

The psalm according to Andreas. Concerning the winepresses. Formerly there was one wine-press, that is to say, there was one temple and one altar in Jerusalem. In the Messiah there are wine-presses, that is to say, many churches everywhere. Lord, (v.1) i.e. the Messiah. Our Lord, (v.1) i.e. he is Lord of everything by nature as is freely admitted; our Lord he is called, impersonating those who believe in him of their own
accord. In all the earth, (v.1) i.e. not in Judea alone but on the whole globe. Thou hast set thy glory above the heavens, (v.1) i.e. you have no glory now, but it is eternal, because you are eternal, and thou hast given of it to the angels which he calls heaven. From the mouth of babes, (v.2) i.e. this was fulfilled in Jerusalem when he entered it according to the gospel; spiritually: from the mouth of those that are innocent of evil. Thou hast established thy glory for thyself, (v.2) i.e. a new (glory). The enemy who seeks to avenge, (v.2) i.e. Judas was the new enemy. The enemy who seeks to avenge, (v.2) i.e. Satan and the demons and death. These seek to avenge us because they seek to subjugate us that we might commit sin, and then on account of it we would be tormented. Or again because they are the cause that God seeks to avenge us. Because they see thy heavens, (v.3) i.e. the angels. The work........, (v.3) i.e. this world and all that is in it and Adam who was created by the hand of God. Fingers, (v.3) i.e. he calls the word and the spirit, for if by the finger of God I cast out the demons; therefore, he that is acclaimed by the children, has established the heavens; therefore, God is he, that enters Jerusalem. The prophecy resumes and speaks because of the father. What is man that thou shouldest remember him?, (v.4) i.e. Paul says that he who was made a little less than the angels is the Messiah. Thou hast made him a little less........, (v.5)
i.e. because he suffered and died for us in the flesh, it is written that he was made less. With honor and glory thou hast endowed him, (v.5) i.e. he was endowed with honor and glory by the resurrection and the veneration by the dead and the living. Thou madest him to rule...., (v.6) i.e. everything was subjugated to him and placed under his feet. The sheep, (v.7) i.e. the simple people and the lowly of heart who believe of Israel. The cattle, that is to say, the oxen, (v.7) i.e. the apostles and prophets and teachers. The animals of the field, (v.7) i.e. the gentiles that are likened to animals in their manners of living. The birds of the heavens, (v.7) i.e. the souls of the righteous or the angels or those men who ponder lofty things. The fish of the sea, (v.8) i.e. the souls in sheol to which is likened the sea and the seas (v.8) because of the many variations in it which are given according to the morals. That cross the paths..., (v.8) i.e. there is one path, that is to say, one death (comes) to all; and it is the path on which they cross from here thither. These (words) of David, Paul interprets, and not that the son is less than the father by nature, are these said, but because of his life in the flesh. Just as kings who share equally in their subjects, although the subjects are one by nature, both fathers and sons, so also is the nature of the father one with the son. Lord, our Lord, (v.9) i.e. he repeats the words at the end of the psalm admiringly and teaches that when creation did not exist, the son was in glory with his father and before the incarnation. Again he is glorified by the spiritual essences; so also after they came to be and he was made man and saved us, glory was not added to him by
means of the praise of (religious creatures, but he abundantly deserved that we praise him who created and saved (us). The psalm according to the LXX. The churches are named wine-presses, in as much as the teachers produce grapes for them and gather fruits from the Lord's vineyard. The altars are called wine-presses because the offerings of all are brought to them and in them spiritual and mystical wine is pressed. From the mouth of babes, (v.2) i.e. babes he calls the sinners who after sucking the rational milk of the sacrament, (redound to) the glory of God, that is to say, they establish praise by their conversion. Babes and sucklings he calls them that believe in the Messiah and the new people that begins in knowledge. A suckling is he that is baptized in knowledge; babes, as (we read): be converted and become as children. Because they see thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, (v.3) i.e. I see the heavens and the stars and the rest of the great and marvelous creatures, but these are the small ones of thy works; works of thy fingers they are, but not of thy hands or of great power, but as a man speaks of the tips of his fingers, so the powers of God are named with which he created the creatures.. Fingers, furthermore, he calls the commandments of God, because as we work with the fingers, so he created with a command. But he says I see, impersonating thereby the nations that did not know that the stars and the sun were a work of God, but having been taught and having seen, that the Messiah with his fingers opened the eyes of the blind, they
understood from the signs below that he had created also the stars. What is man that thou shouldest remember him, (v.4) i.e. in comparison to the divine nature man is nothing. Or the son of man that thou visitest him, (v.4) i.e. although God visits the entire creation, yet man, having sinned through the flesh which he took from him, he visited when he came. Thou hast made him a little less, (v.5) i.e. it was little becoming to him that he was in sheol three days and suffered for us. The angels are immortal, we are mortal; yet we have been crowned with praise of honors by this: let us make man in our image and likeness. Everything thou hast subjected under his feet, (v.6) i.e. although he is above humanity in its entirety, yet it was meet for the Messiah in the flesh that all should be subjected to him. The birds of the heavens, (v.8) i.e. those that are occupied with theology and search out divine things. The fish of the sea, (v.8) i.e. those that swim in the affairs of the world as in waves, and they also are saved when they cross the paths not of the sea but of the seas (v.8) i.e. when they walk by baptism and repentance. Lord, our Lord, how wondrous........, (v.9)
i.e. the Messiah is admired everywhere; he returns to the mentioning of the praise of God because he also has referred often to the love of humanity of God.

The ninth Psalm. Concerning the hidden things of the son, i.e. those that came about by his life in the flesh, as the conception and birth when he was hidden from Satan. That I might show forth all of thy wonders, (v.1) i.e. wonders are of two kinds: one is the creation which, from that which was not, came into being, and (things) similar to it; the other: wonders that he did when he was made man: the conception without seed and the birth from a virgin and the cleansing of the lepers and the rest of the miracles. When my enemies turn back, (v.3) i.e. the demons from whom was taken the name of godliness and who were crushed and who turned back from before him when he descended into sheol and vanquished death. For thou hast accomplished my revenge, (v.4) i.e. as (we read): now is the judgment of the world. Thou sittest upon the throne, (v.4) i.e. when he appeared in the flesh, and thou hast gained the victory and hast judged and hast saved. Thou hast rebuked the nations, (v.5) i.e. the demons, as (we read): Jesus rebuked him and said: depart from him. My enemies have perished by the sword, (v.6) i.e. those demons and their wiles and their corrupting thoughts are
killed by the sword which is the word of God which is sharper than a two-edged sword, and these (things) through the apostles who received this authority. Towns thou hast destroyed and effaced....., (v.6) i.e. the habitation of the demons in the hearts, and again in sheol and the dwelling-places in it. He hath prepared his throne for judgment, (v.7) i.e. that examination when he judges by fire and tests all flesh by it. The Lord will be a refuge for the needy, (v.9) i.e. for the poor of spirit that hear: come, ye blessed of my father. And their helper in the time of distress, (v.9) i.e. when they are delivered from the time of distress of this world, and even if in the day of judgment. And all..... will believe in thee, (v.10) i.e. by faith they bear their evils in this world until they reach the true (world). Sing unto the Lord who dwells in Zion, (v.11) i.e. in the church or in that (Zion) which is in heaven and not in that (Zion) on which he was lifted on the cross. Declare his schemes among the nations, (v.11) (schemes) he calls those (things) that he performed in his life which were hidden from Satan. For he schemed against him in the body in order to consummate what he, who had made himself like a serpent, had done to Adam, and as the scripture says: with the wound, with which he wounded him, he wounded him and with the killing, with which he killed him, he killed him. Because he remembered to avenge their blood, (v.12) i.e. of Adam and Eve whom he killed with sin, and of the fathers and the saints that were killed because
of him. The cry of the needy......, (v.12) i.e. the human nature whose cry he did not forget. My servitude by those who hate me, (v.13) i.e. the demons. O thou, who liftest me up from the gates of death, (v.13) i.e. from that of sin and from natural death in the resurrection. I will tell........ thy wonders, (v.14) i.e. the wonders by God in Jerusalem. In the gates of the daughter of Zion, (v.14) i.e. these are the holy apostles. They lock up the gentiles, (v.15) i.e. the demons (lock up) those that are cast into hell. The Lord proclaims judgment........, (v.16) i.e. to the heavenly powers and everyone that is under the heavens. The wicked shall turn back to sheol, (v.17) i.e. the demons and unbelievers. The needy shall not be forgotten forever, (v.18) i.e. for the hope of the spiritually humble shall not perish, who for its sake have entered the narrow gate and endured earthly torments. Arise, Lord, and do not let man prevail, (v.19) i.e. he that is the tool of the demons for evil, and they have forsaken God. Raise up for them the law, (v.20) i.e. in the place of the Old Testament he established the New which is the son. That the nations may know, (v.20) i.e. that they may understand that they were created in the likeness of God and that they are not like animals and oxen because of their manner of life. From Andrew concerning the hidden things of the son, i.e. that he performed them in a hidden way: the birth in the flesh from a virgin, and the miracles which he did,
and the death and the resurrection- these, and those like these, he did hidden from the great of this world. This psalm speaks allegorically of the death of our Lord. The LXX, in superscription, characterize this thing as hidden because this mystery was unknown also to the apostles to the end, and this is the thing that was written: it was hidden from their eyes. I will confess the Lord with all my heart, (v.1) i.e. for it is not meet that the confession be partial, lest the forgiveness be partial, for also when we hide sores from the doctor, then from the half, that we are sick of, we recover; hence this that we confess with all our hearts (occurs) when we do not turn to sins again for which we have asked forgiveness. I will declare all thy wonders, (v.1) i.e. for after we have confessed and by confession are pure, then we will declare the wonders that God has done to us. I will rejoice and exult in thee and sing thy name, (v.2) i.e. those that are called to faith in the Messiah, acknowledge him when they sing and rejoice in him, in as much as they no longer rejoice in idols. They shall fall and perish before thy face, (v.3) i.e. the face of the father is the son; Satan is debilitated and his powers by him. Again they will be debilitated by thy face, i.e. by means of the likeness that thou hast placed upon me. Thou sittest upon the throne, (v.4) i.e. not hast thou neglected the human nature, but like a man that sits upon a throne and judges, torment such as this thou hast brought upon the evil one in order that his memory may be blotted out. Thou hast rebuked the nations, (v.5) i.e. the demons. And thou hast
destroyed the wicked, (v.5) i.e. the devil, in as much as he overtops the demons. And their names thou hast blotted out, (v.5) i.e. not as having disappeared in complete extinction, but that he now is not able to harm as in the beginning, for his power is extinguished as by the preaching of the apostles. And their names thou hast blotted out, (v.5) i.e. the glory and honor of the demons, for when jealousy and adultery and sins do not rule over us, then the name of Satan is blotted out. My enemies have come to an end by the sword forever, (v.6) i.e. the Greek: the spears of the enemy have come to an end, i.e. the spears and arrows are the sins with which the devil strikes, but when the Messiah vanquished him, he fled and there came to an end his passions with which he would kill us. The towns thou hast uprooted, (v.6) i.e. the demons he calls cities and towns which tremble and fall. Again otherwise: these who were his instruments and weapons for sin, are the (morally excellent and they rose up against him; the towns in which sin was cultivated are converted to the worship of God. Thou hast destroyed their memory, (v.6) the Greek: their memory perishes with tumult, i.e. the memory and remembrance of Satan is idol-worship, and this has perished with tumult when the idols and their altars fell. The Lord shall endure forever, (v.7) i.e. his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. And he will judge the world in truth, (v.8) i.e. the church he calls the world inasmuch as it has been altogether evangelised.
and the nations in it. Peoples (he calls) the rest outside the church. A refuge for the needy......., (v.9) i.e. the human nature he calls needy because it was made needy by the transgression of the commandment. Again, a father indeed, denies (his) needy son, likewise a brother (his) needy brother, God, however, (is) not thus, but he gives his riches to the needy when by grace he took on need. Sing praises to the Lord who dwells in Zion, (v.11) i.e. in every soul which is Zion, that is to say, a watch-tower, the Lord dwells. Show his schemes among the nations, (v.11) i.e. the Hebrew: the preparations, that is to say, his preparations he calls places that the Messiah visited when he was made flesh, allegorical and literal. Because he remembered to avenge their blood, (v.11) i.e. those who were killed by the arrows of the devil through idolatry, and by means of his cross he has avenged their vengeance. He did not forget the cry of the needy, (v.12) i.e. the gentiles are the needy because they do not have the law or the prophets. With unspoken groanings they pray to God, looking expectantly for his help. O thou, who liftest me out of the gates of death, (v.13) i.e. the demons are called the gates of death because they lead those who are in subjection to them down to sheol. The gates of death are sins from which he is lifted up who is adorned with excellence. Again the gates of death are adultery, stealing, jealousy and the like; from these the Messiah raised us up through his coming. That I may show...... thy glories in the gates of the daughter of Zion, (v.14) i.e. by repentance and baptism; these are the gates of the church, that is to say, Zion, that is to say, glories are thanks-
giving. Zion he calls the church which is the daughter of Jerusalem in heaven and that of the church of the first-born. Again Zion he calls the heavenly city. The gates, therefore, of it belong to the churches on earth in which we rejoice. We will rejoice in thy salvation, (v.14) i.e. salvation he calls the Messiah, as (we read): for my eyes have seen thy salvation, that is to say, the Messiah when Simeon saw him. The nations are sunk down in destruction, (v.15) i.e. the nations he calls the demons when they prepared the cross for the Messiah. Through this they fell from their tyranny. Again the nations are sunk down, i.e. the heathen that killed the saints, and by the death of the martyrs preaching was confirmed. By the work of his hands there is snared ......, (v.16) i.e. for the wicked devil prepared the sign of the cross for our Savior but by it he is snared, for he is trodden under the feet of the holy ones. Not completely is to be forgotten the needy, (v.18) for he will not come to grief by the long delay of the judgment but unto the end, praising, he will be saved. Therefore, the long delay he calls forgetting. Arise, Lord, (v.19) i.e. help those who are fallen under the passions and fetters of Satan. And do not let man prevail, (v.19) i.e. the devil. He calls him man, as being weak and earthly. And let the nations be judged before......, (v.19) i.e. the judge says: come now let us reason together, and if your sins are as scarlet, I will make them white as wool. Raise up for them a
law-giver, (v.20) i.e. the Messiah who was born in the flesh; when the nations received him, they knew that they are men. And it is meet that they be cleansed of their passions because they lived like animals in bestial passions and afterwards, through the Messiah, they were elevated to intelligence, meet for men.

Psalm 10. Why standest thou afar off, O Lord? (v.1) i.e. who dost thou delay thy coming while the devil imposes his yoke upon everyone? Why dost thou stand afar off, O Lord?- among the Greeks it is one with the previous psalm; among the Syrians it is separate. We in this interpretation like the Greeks have treated it as one, but like the Syrians we will interpret it separately again below. Why hast thou removed afar off?- says the word with the Lord, since the grace of God expects the repentance of sinners. For sin removes God afar off, as (we read): your sins have separated between thee and me. At the arrogance of the wicked the needy is incensed, (v.2) i.e. for when the righteous sees that the wicked prospers, he is incensed by his thoughts since Satan incites the righteous to imitate jealously the transgression of the law. The wicked is blessed, but the Lord is angry, (v.3) i.e. those that praise the wicked are those that incite them to sin the more, as those that call evil wisdom (and) contempt humility. The sinner has provoked the Lord, (v.4) i.e. for it is clear that, persevering in sin, he does not permit God to deal with him with human kindliness, but
he looses the grace of God. In his great anger he will not prosecute, (v.4) i.e. if the prosecution is like the anger, the evil will perish immediately. God is not in any of his thoughts (v.4) and his ways perish, (v.5) i.e. he does not place God before his eyes; all of his deeds and his manner of living and the ways of his life he makes unclean and impure. Thy judgment is high above him, (v.5) i.e. he completely disregards thy laws (and) spends all his time in the transgression of the law. He despises all his enemies, (v.5) i.e. the devil despises the enemies of God and those who are subjugated to him in sin. He says in his heart: I shall not be moved forever, (v.6) i.e. they (the words) indicate the untruthfulness of the devil. He sits lurkingly in the den and the rest, (v.8) i.e. with these (words) he alludes to the devil and he likens him to a lion who seizes. He says in his heart: God has forgotten. (v.8) i.e. the devil says these (words) intending that he forgets not him but us in order that we might take offense, thinking that God disregards these human affairs. Arise Lord and raise thy hand, (v.12) i.e. the wicked are of the opinion that thou sleepest because of thy patience. Hand he calls the Messiah who for the deliverance of sinners was manifested. Wherefore does the sinner provoke God,? (v.13) i.e. sinner he calls the devil or a wicked person
who falsely accuses God, that he does not concern himself about the world. Upon thee the poor is cast, (v.14) i.e. that thou make him rich. Thou art the helper of the orphan, (v.14) i.e. orphan he calls him whose father for a time was the devil, and now he has forsaken him since he repented of his sins. Break the arm of the sinner, (v.15) i.e. crush the power of the unjust. The sin of the evil one will be prosecuted and he will not be found, (v.15) i.e. for if the sin of him who has committed evils is examined, he will not be found because of it. i.e. he has justly perished. For where is the pomp of Pharaoh and the greed of Judas? With the fruit also the root-stock has perished. The Lord will reign forever, (v.16) i.e. sin is reigning; for when it has perished, then God will reign over the sinners forever. The nations have perished from his earth, (v.16) i.e. those that remain in sin will perish being cast into hell. The hope of the needy, (v.17) i.e. those that are in poverty of error he calls needy because they acquire the riches of the Messiah and a fine desire and God has heard them. The preparation of their heart, (v.17) i.e. fastings and virtues. The orphans, (v.18) and the poor (v.18) he calls those who till now do not believe
and he prays that the Messiah, the Savior, may be theirs. Again to judge the orphans and the poor, (v.18) i.e. mankind in general he calls thus; Adam had become an orphan when he had fallen from the sonship; needy (he became) when it was decreed that he should return to dust. No more will man boast upon the earth, (v.18) i.e. here he means by man a living, rational, mortal (being) and again, because of his weakness, (he means by man) the devil since he says arrogantly that he possesses the whole universe; for he will not be arrogant when he is trodden under the feet of the righteous.

The 10 Psalm. The Syriac interprets this Psalm apart from the previous one. Why standest thou afar off, O Lord? (v.1) i.e. hasten now to the deliverance and the calling of the nations and deliver them from the oppression of the devil. At the pride of the wicked..., (v.2) i.e. the devil. The needy is incensed, (v.2) i.e. human nature. May they be taken in the device, (v.2) i.e. as (we read): with the wound with which he wounded him he wounded him. The wicked boasts, (v.3) i.e. with these sinful desires (v.3) and they are lauded appearing as divine to the human nature. The wicked is blessed, (v.3) i.e. the devil and he that is worshipped in idols. In his
haughtiness he does not seek out, (v.4) that which is sin, from righteousness, and leave that and do that which is excellent. Thy judgment is far above him, (v.5) i.e. either because he does not profess that there is a judgment or he does know it and contemns it. He despises all his enemies, (v.5) his associates who have become his enemies because he fell. He sits lurkingly in a den, (v.8) that of the mind, lying in hiding in the desires of his flesh. And secretly he kills the righteous, (v.8) i.e. he kills the good intention of the righteous by sin. He will be humbled and he will fall, (v.10) i.e. since our Lord has come and defeated him and taught us to give battle and defeat him. And in his bones, (v.10) i.e. his bones are the demons that are under him. Disease and pains, (v.10) i.e. because our race was liberated from his servitude, they are afflicted with pains and are delivered unto torment and are filled with disease because of their jealousy of us that we were counted worthy of the kingdom. He said in his heart: God has forgotten, (v.11) i.e. the devil was saying, before the incarnation of the Lord, that God had forgotten man and did not concern himself about him. Arise, Lord, and do not let man prevail, i.e. arise, Lord, and destroy the strength of the devil. Thou awaitest that he be delivered, (v.14) i.e. into thy hands, the devil himself, O Lord; and he will not be able to flee but thou art awaiting that the time come that thou shouldest be incarnated and then thou wilt save. The poor and
the needy (v.14, v.16) he calls mankind which was made poor having lost the incorruptibility which was in paradise. Break the arm...., (v.15) i.e. the devil who is the arm of the sinner, (v.15) and he helps them toward sin; for when this is broken, then sin will be sought and not found. The Lord is king, (v.16) i.e. in this world and that which is to come. The nations are perished from (his) earth, (v.16) i.e. the demons that will fall into the fire and will not be worthy of the land of promise. The hope of the needy, (v.17) i.e. that thou wilt give the inheritance to them that expect that the kingdom will be theirs. The preparation of their heart, (v.17) i.e. because their heart prepares for the kingdom, i.e. because their heart prepares for the kingdom. To judge the orphans, (v.18) i.e. those who were oppressed and distressed for his sake. And he will destroy no more, (v.18) and when he does these things he will let the just inherit the kingdom and the wicked damnation that not again they perish from him through the deception of the evil one, as they perished in Eden.

The 11 Psalm. According to the Peshitta version. In the Lord I put my trust, how do you say? (V.1) i.e. he sang this psalm when the army of Saul and those with him prevailed; those that were with David said: justly he is pursued because he arose against Saul and they did not know that he was the anointed of God. In the Lord I put my trust, (v.1) i.e. I will not flee
from trials. For he held out bravely and asked of God that he might pursue after those that captured his wife and his sons; and he went and came upon them when the Amalekite had shown them to him, and he turned the captivity. The psalm denotes allegorically the inner mind of the saints that are assailed by the devil. For sinners....., (v.2) i.e. the demons. They have bent the bow, (v.2) i.e. the wars that they instigate against us through carnal passions. They have aimed their arrows, (v.2) i.e. sins, such as envy and deceit. To shoot in the dark, (v.2) i.e. in order that they may not be seen, or many are wounded by the arrows and do not know that they are committing sin, such as the proud and the envious and the mockers. Because whatever thou preparest, they destroy, (v.3) i.e. whereas thou hadst created man and placed him in paradise that he should not die, they destroyed and killed (him). The righteous, therefore, what will he do,? (v.3) he therefore, that seeks to be righteous, what will he do because they do not cease waging war. The Lord is in his holy temple, (v.4) i.e. he encourages him not to be moved by the war, saying: the Lord is in heaven, i.e. in his temple. And to him will the righteous look that he come to his help. His eyes see, (v.4) i.e. he does not forget anything. Again, his eyes are the angels that are sent for ministration for the sake of those that are going to inherit life. His eyes are trying, (v.4) i.e. his judgments are trying i.e. they are seeking out.
The Lord will try the righteous, (v.5) i.e. he will permit the righteous to be persecuted, as it were, for purification. The wicked and the lovers of wickedness, (v.5) i.e. he will hate the wicked on the day when he shall say: depart, ye cursed, into the fire. Snares like rain....., (v.6) i.e. as he that is on the field is not able to flee from the rain, so those from not falling into snares, i.e. into unquenchable fire. A terrible tempest, (v.6) i.e. of judgment. According to the LXX. In the end, is placed in the title of the preceding psalm,in as much as in the later times the Messiah had come and helped men, and after the trials that he met with or in the end he spoke it. Again being persecuted by Saul, he spoke it when they counseled him that he should flee and obtain deliverance. It is fitting for everyone that is persecuted and that trusts in God. The end is written over it as showing the sentence of judgment and torment that is coming upon the trespassers of the law. In the Lord have I trusted, (v.1) i.e. these words the prophet says to those that consoled him in his trials. How do you say to my soul? (V.1) i.e. (to the soul) of those that trust in God. Flee to the mountain like a bird, (v.1) i.e. it is meet for the excellent that they fly away and dwell on holy mountains. Mountains he calls the prophets. It is meet for those who exercise virtues that they walk in the footsteps of these. Again, it is meet for those who trust in the Lord that they fly away upon mountains, that is, virtues, since they have nothing to do with anything
that creeps on the ground. In these mountains, that is, virtues, we cast off from us the mire of lusts. Upon the mountains like a bird, i.e. why do you advise me to flee and to go hither and thither upon mountains like a bird that is afraid, since I trust in God who, perfect in conduct, has this word: nothing shall be able to separate him from the love of God, neither distress nor need. They draw the bow, (v.2) i.e. the sinners. They are evil men that pursue the righteous, also demons. They draw he says and not they shoot; they draw, but are not able to place the arrow on it because God makes them ineffectual. The demon attacks man with adultery and shoots with lust at the heart. But he that trusts in the Lord, after the manner of a bird flees to the mountain and overcomes evil. To shoot in darkness, (v.2) i.e. in the LXX: darkness without the moon, that is, that (darkness) under the moon he means. At that time the demon sinners attack; they are not able to shoot at the righteous in the light. For he is not wounded who has in his mind the light of God. He is shot who is in darkness and surrounded by a cloud of sloth. Because anything that thou hast prepared, (v.3) i.e. those laws and commandments of God which he has instituted for our salvation, the demons break down through our transgression. The righteous, now, what will he do? (V.3) i.e. the righteous here he calls the son when he saw the devil who harmed us by reason of our sloth. His eyes see, (v.4) i.e. when the eyes of the shepherd look
upon the lamb, they guard the flock and put to flight the wolves. When one wishes to visit the needy, one uses the eyes righteously. His eyelids try, (v.4) i.e. at the time of the judgment with the eyelids, as indicating the threat. The snares shall come down on the wicked, (v.6) i.e. offences and stumbling-blocks he will send upon them in order that they be convicted of sin and go to God. Fire and brimstone, etc., (v.6) i.e. The portion of their cup, (v.6) i.e. by the word cup he alludes to all their punishments; the fire indicates the threat by burning; brimstone (indicates) the thing that still more stirs up the fire; the hurricane (indicates) the return of some tribulations. Because the Lord is righteous and righteousness......, (v.7) i.e. as he is righteous, thus he is delighted by the saints; so he is delighted by righteousness and according to the righteousness of everyone he recompenses. His countenance beholds uprightness, (v.7) i.e. equity, when he shall exalt the righteous that are humbled and cast down the wicked, that were exalted, to the devil in torment.

The 12 Psalm. The interpretation according to the Peshitta. Deliver, Lord, for the good is extinct, (v.1) i.e. from the earth. And faith has ceased, (v.1) i.e. (faith) of men. God has revealed himself upon the earth in the flesh and saved the world. Because the good was extinct, iniquity ruled; and when iniquity has sway, all the seeds of excellence cease. With a heart and a heart, (v.2) i.e. therefore with a divided heart and with a deceitful tongue men teach, and especially they who
saw the miracles of the Lord and heard the prophecy concerning our Savior. Who say: with our tongue we shall boast, (v.4) i.e. how were they not boasters (v.3) who said: through Beelzebub he casts out the demons, and by what authority dost thou do these? The lips are ours; who... (v.4) i.e. and these, fancying that the authority was theirs, therefore said: this one, we know not whence he is. Because of the despoiling of the needy, (v.5) i.e. who are (so) in spirit. Therefore I will arise, (v.5) i.e. I will become man, I will save, I will die, I will descend to sheol, I will restore the souls, I will arise from the dead. I will make a salvation, (v.5) i.e. I will make a salvation publicly (v.5) i.e. for all the world, for the dead as well as the living. The saying of the Lord, (v.6) i.e. either the prophecy concerning the son or the son himself who is named the word. Choice silver (v.6) he said and not gold, teaching that prophecy is inferior to the apostleship, and with silver, that is, prophecy the prophet proclaims to all of his. Which was tried in the earth, (v.6) i.e. the earth, in which the prophecy was tried, he calls the church and the souls of the saints and of the true teachers. These wise money-changers understood the words that the words; that the prophets had spoken concerning him and searched and knew that he was God. Purged seven times,
(v.6) i.e. because seven are the operations of the spirit, that is, by which the mind is purified and understands the truth, as is said: no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Spirit. But thou, O Lord, shalt keep them, (v.7) i.e. from the enemy hosts and evil men. Deliver me from this generation, (v.7) i.e. from that one which arose against the Messiah. The wicked circle about, i.e. the Jews. Like the licentious height of the sons of Edom, (v.8) i.e. these Edomites are the sons of Esau and they worship the image of Aphrodite and it was placed upon a certain height i.e. a hill; and on the feast of Aphrodite in the temple which was there, as an honor for the goddess of lust, they interpret her; they act lewdly, and there women and virgins and men and youths madly commit fornication. The interpretation of the same psalm according to the version of the LXX. The import of the psalm: there is an accusation in it against every unjust and wicked and two-minded and other-willed and deceiver by a word and him that commits sacrilege upon the altar and that increases through deceit. It reproves those that employ duplicity and profess love, but desire to betray David to Saul and show where he dwells. There is inscribed over it: for the eight, because he mentions the judgment that God executed after the seventh; in the end, i.e. at the end of time, and in it he shows the abrogation of the Sabbath; because he that is born on the Sabbath, is circumcised thus on the eight (day). He alludes to the first day of the week, because the first and the eight is
the cleansing of every soul. Save me, O Lord, because the pious is extinct, (v.1) i.e. there is not left a pious one among men that can save me, therefore thou, O Lord, be a deliverer to me because evil is strongly armed against me. This prayer, again, the human nature was offering at the time of suffering when no pious man was found: Judas was a traitor, the priests oppressors, the scribes liars. Truth diminishes of men, (v.1) i.e. because of the fear of the Jews, that is, as the father of the blind man feared to confess that the Messiah opened his eyes. Again, the heathen speak deception who have forsaken God and worship the work of their hands. Everyone speaks vanities, (v.2) i.e. when they were preparing plots against our Savior and were speaking with a deceitful heart with him. Again, vanities are the stories of the heathen. Again, they put on the appearance of love but do the acts of enemies. Deceitful lips, (v.2) i.e. the lips agree with the heart and the heart with the lips. The thinking and the tongue of the Jews was full of treachery; for that reason with tempting they drew near to the Messiah. The Lord shall destroy the lips, (v.3) i.e. when the Lord blots out the evils, which are an accident, there will appear the creation of God for which these were accidents. Not another but the Lord can overcome the cruelty of the Jews, that not again they blaspheme the Savior, therefore
destruction did not come upon the lips but upon the power and the working of the evil. Tongues that boast, (v.3) i.e. the priest and the people who say to the Messiah: with what authority dost thou do these? who has given to thee authority? Because of the despoiling of the needy and the groaning, (v.5) i.e. the poor he calls the prophets and the apostles and believers who are needy in their will, and these he delivered from that wretchedness and groaning that (is caused) by the Jews by hastening the resurrection. The saying of the Lord, (v.6) i.e. the commandments and the teachings of the gospel. The heretical teachings are not pure, but defiled. Choice silver, (v.6) i.e. as silver is purged two and three times by smelting, so also the sayings of the Lord are full of truth. And thou shalt deliver us from this generation, (v.7). The church prays to the Messiah to be delivered by faith in this age, that is, in this generation from sin, and in the world to come from torment. The wicked round about, (v.8) i.e. the demons surround the righteous, but thou, O Lord, preserve us from them. Like a summit thou increaseth the hours of all men, (v.8). The great number of hours indicates the great amount of time and the endless world after this one.

The 13 Psalm. To the end by David. He sang this when he was in repentance for sins. He shows in it both the turning away
of God from the human nature and the sadness that the saints felt concerning the expulsion of Adam from paradise: Enoch, Noah, and the descendants of Abraham and the rest of the prophets. How long will my enemy exalt himself? (V.2) i.e. the devil, sin, death. Look upon and answer me, (v.3) i.e. the look of the father is the son who by his incarnation was able to enlighten the eyes of the saints. Enlighten my eyes, (v.3) i.e. that they do not sleep in sheol as unto death. And let not my enemy say, (v.4) i.e. the Messiah descended to the saints and delivered them and overpowered the serpent that seduced us in the beginning. And this he did when he arose from the grave. And (lest) my oppressors rejoice over me, (v.4) i.e. the demons. When I shall tremble, (v.4) i.e. the trembling of death, as it is said: he will liberate those who through fear of death were subject to bondage all their life. Of the same psalm: this psalm David spoke concerning himself when he was pursued by Absalom. These of Saul were before the sin; therefore, they were spoken with boldness; these of Absalom after the sin, and therefore weeping and groaning were joined with the words. How long wilt thou forget me, (v.1) i.e. the delay of help he names forgetting. He petitions that he be not forgotten to the end, lest he be entirely deprived of divine providence. How long wilt thou turn thy face, (v.1) i.e. those who are angry with someone do not want to look upon him. The face of the Lord is full of light, and if he turns his face from anyone, he remains in darkness of the soul. How long shall I place
reflections in my soul, (v.2) i.e. he asks a purging of the soul and the heart lest he be prone to vile pleasures. And misery in my heart every day, (v.2) i.e. misery of the heart and of the day he names the deceiving thoughts. For the thoughts of sin are ulcers of the soul. How long will (my enemy) exalt himself over me, (v.2) i.e. the exaltation of Satan is the humiliation of men through sins, because as God is said to be glorified by our salvation, so the devil (is said to be) exalted by our destruction. Look upon and answer me, (v.3) i.e. there comes first: look upon, and afterwards: answer. For it is customary, before the words, to seek correction of those that pray, and sacrifices are pleasing to him, not those only that (come) from the tongue, but those that (come) from the right hand and offer alms. Enlighten my eyes lest I sleep, (v.3) i.e. sleep he names the sloth by which, as if in dreams, we go astray by the illusions of the world. They make us idle in order that we fall upon the bed of voluptuousness. Let not my enemy say: I have overcome him, (v.4) i.e. the rejoicers in iniquity are the enemies who oppress the saints, and they exult if it happens that they sin, whether mentally or perceptibly. I have trusted in thy mercy, (v.5) i.e. for he that trusts in the mercy of God, should show mercy toward his brother and neighbor. My heart exults in thy salvation, (v.5) i.e. salvation is the son. When, being filled
with virtues, am I to be worthy to inherit thy salvation? I will praise the Lord who has helped me, (v.6) i.e. I will worship and praise thee for all the help from thee.
